scenarios.title: {Pf} Meets the Squad
text: The club's family day. {Pf} is meeting the squad's partners for the first time, and the captain's wife is famously terrifying.
There's a players-and-partners dinner tonight. {Pf} has changed outfits three times and asked eleven questions about who sits where.

choices.label: Stay by her side all night
choices.hint: She'll feel safe. The lads will tease you.
choices.text: He doesn't leave her side once. The squad calls him 'the bodyguard' for a week. {Pf} calls it the best night since they met.

out.text: She's a hit. By dessert she's in the partners' group chat and knows more club gossip than he does.
She's left alone with the captain's wife for forty minutes. In the car she says, 'Never again.'

scenarios.title: The Fan Who Got Too Close
text: A fan at the gate kisses {J} on the cheek during a selfie. Someone films it. {Pf} has seen it before he has.
A model comments a heart-eyes emoji under every one of {J}'s posts. {Pf} has noticed. She hasn't said anything. That's the problem.

choices.label: Bring it up first
choices.text: He shows her the video before she can mention it. She laughs, mostly with relief. 'Thank you for telling me.'

choices.label: Block the account publicly
choices.hint: She'll love it. The internet will talk.
choices.text: He blocks the account and posts a photo with {Pf}. The internet goes wild. So does {Pf}, in a good way.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: He says nothing. She says nothing. The silence lasts three days and is very loud.

scenarios.title: Surprise Dinner
text: {J} decides to surprise {Pf} with a home-cooked dinner. He has watched one video. The kitchen has never been in more danger.
{Pf} comes home to candles, music, and a smoke alarm going off.

choices.label: Order takeaway, keep the candles
choices.text: They eat {FOOD} from boxes by candlelight on the floor. She says it's the most romantic thing he's ever done. He thinks she might mean it.

choices.label: Serve it anyway
choices.text: She eats every bite with a straight face, then admits she's never been prouder or more frightened.

scenarios.title: {Pf}'s Big News
text: {Pf} has been offered a promotion at work. It's in another city. She's excited and terrified and watching his face very carefully.
{Pf} wants to go back to university. Evenings and weekends. Exactly when he's free.

choices.label: 'Do it. We'll make it work.'
choices.text: She hugs him so hard he loses his breath. It'll be complicated. They'll make it work.

choices.label: 'Can we talk about the timing?'
choices.text: They talk for two hours. She says she understands. She's quieter for a week.

scenarios.title: The Dating App
text: {T} has secretly made {J} a dating profile. It has a terrible photo and a bio that says 'professional ball kicker, looking for a striker partner'. It has 400 matches.
{BFf} insists {J} tries a dating app. The first match asks if he can get her tickets.

choices.label: Give it a real go
choices.hint: Love, chaos or a screenshot in the papers.

out.text: One conversation stands out: funny, sharp, no football questions. They meet for coffee. Her name is {P}.
A week of conversations about his salary. He deletes the app.
Someone screenshots his profile and posts it. 'Professional ball kicker' trends for a day.

choices.label: Delete it, get revenge
choices.text: He deletes it and fills {T}'s car with balloons. The dressing room approves of the escalation.

scenarios.title: The Plus-One Problem
text: {CAPl}'s wedding invitation says '{J} + 1'. {J} does not have a +1. The whole squad is bringing partners.
A cousin's wedding. {MUM} has 'arranged' for him to sit next to a family friend's daughter. She has done this before.

choices.label: Bring {BFf}
choices.text: {BFf} wears a suit two sizes too big and dances with every grandmother. He's the star of the wedding.

out.text: Against all odds, they get on brilliantly. They talk all evening. Her name is {P}. {MUM} is unbearable about it.
Polite conversation about the weather for four hours. {MUM} asks for a full report. There's nothing to report.

scenarios.title: Coffee on the Journalist
text: Walking into the press room, {J} trips on a cable and spills coffee all over {JR} from {OUT}. On his notebook. On his laptop.
In the mixed zone {J} turns too fast and his water bottle drenches {JR}'s recorder.

choices.label: Replace everything, personally
choices.hint: Expensive. A friend in the press.
choices.text: {J} sends a new laptop the next day with a note. {JR} writes about it in his column, kindly. The press room loves the story.

choices.label: Apologise and laugh it off
choices.text: {JR} is gracious. Mostly. His next piece is noticeably less warm.

scenarios.title: Podcast Invitation
text: A popular football podcast wants {J} on next week. Two former players, a lot of laughing, and a reputation for getting guests to say things they regret.
A comedy podcast, not even a football one, wants {J} as a guest. Their last athlete guest admitted he hates his club's kit.

out.text: He's funny, warm and honest. Clips spread everywhere. Fans who didn't know him now love him.
He's funny — a bit too funny about {Mf}'s training methods. The clip makes the back pages.

choices.label: Go on, keep it media-trained
choices.text: He gives careful answers. The hosts are a bit disappointed. The club's media team is delighted.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: He declines politely. They book someone else, who says something stupid. {J} feels lucky.

scenarios.title: The Unflattering Photo
text: A fan's selfie with {J} catches him mid-sneeze. It's the least flattering photo of a human ever taken. It's going viral as a meme template.
A photo of {J} mid-celebration, face twisted into something prehistoric, has become a reaction meme. It's everywhere.

choices.label: Make it your profile picture
choices.text: He makes it his profile picture. The internet decides he's 'one of us'. Followers pour in.

choices.label: Ask for it to be taken down
choices.text: Asking makes it worse. Now there are memes about the meme.

scenarios.title: A Quote He Never Said
text: A fake quote is spreading: '{J}: I'd leave {club} tomorrow for a bigger club.' He has never said this. It's on a graphic with his face.
A parody account with a convincing name has 'quoted' {J} insulting the fans of {R}. It has twenty thousand retweets.

choices.label: Post a clear denial
choices.text: His denial travels almost as fast as the lie. Almost.

choices.label: Let the club handle it
choices.text: The club's statement is formal and slow. The fake quote has already done some damage.

choices.label: Call {JR} to debunk it
choices.hint: Depends on your relationship with the press.

ok.text: {JR} runs a debunk piece within the hour. Other outlets follow. The lie dies quickly.

bad.text: {JR} says he'll 'look into it'. By the time he does, everyone has moved on — to believing the lie.

scenarios.title: Lunch With the President
text: President {PRES} invites {J} to lunch in the directors' suite. White tablecloths, three forks, and a very long story about the president's golf handicap.
{PRESl}'s assistant calls: the president would like {J} to join a sponsors' lunch. Dress code: 'smart'. {J} owns one suit.

choices.label: Charm the room
choices.hint: Board points. Some teammates will call it sucking up.
choices.text: He laughs at every golf story. By dessert, {PRESl} is calling him 'the future of this club'. {CAPl} raises an eyebrow when he hears.

choices.label: Be honest about the squad's concerns

out.text: {PRESl} listens, takes notes, and actually fixes the broken gym equipment the next week. The squad hears who raised it.
{PRESl}'s smile goes stiff. 'Football matters, {J}. Let's keep to football.'

scenarios.title: The Parking Space
text: {J} has parked in the space marked 'Director'. It was the only one free. A director has arrived and is standing next to his car, phone in hand.
There's a note on {J}'s windscreen. It's from a board member. It is very polite and very, very angry.

choices.label: Run out and apologise
choices.text: He apologises three times. The director accepts and then mentions it at the next board meeting anyway.

choices.label: Leave a signed shirt as an apology
choices.text: The director frames the shirt. The parking incident becomes a funny story he tells at sponsor dinners.

scenarios.title: The Ultras' Clubhouse
text: The leader of the ultras group invites {J} to their clubhouse: a room above a garage, flags on every wall, a drum the size of a car tyre.
The ultras are painting a giant banner for Sunday and want {J} to add a brushstroke. They say it's tradition. It isn't. They just invented it.

choices.label: Go and stay for hours
choices.hint: Fans adore you. The board worry about the photos.
choices.text: He drinks sweet tea, learns three new chants and bangs the drum. The ultras adopt him. A photo of him in their scarf makes the board uneasy.

choices.label: Drop in for ten minutes
choices.text: Ten minutes, a brushstroke, photos, handshakes. Everyone's happy.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: The ultras take it badly. There's a pointed silence when he warms up on Sunday.

scenarios.title: {T}'s Secret
text: {T} pulls {J} aside, eyes red. He's been gambling. A lot. Nobody knows. He's begging {J} not to tell anyone.
{T} admits, in the car park, that he's been struggling with his mental health for months. He hasn't told the club.

choices.label: Keep the secret, help him yourself
choices.text: {J} spends evenings with him, helps him find a counsellor quietly. It's draining. {T} will never forget it.

choices.label: Persuade him to tell the club

out.text: After a long night of talking, {T} agrees. The club's support staff are excellent. He thanks {J} weeks later.
{T} feels betrayed even by the suggestion. He stops talking to {J}.

scenarios.title: {BFf} Turns Up
text: {BFf} turns up unannounced with a backpack and a grin. He's taken a 14-hour bus. He's staying 'a few days'.
There's a knock at the door at 23:00. It's {BFf}, holding a bag of {FOOD} from the stall back home. 'Surprise.'

choices.label: Show him your whole life
choices.text: {BFf} meets the squad, eats in the canteen, does a lap of the empty stadium. He doesn't say much, but he takes a photo of everything.

choices.label: Evenings only
choices.text: They spend evenings on the sofa watching {SHOW} like they're fifteen. It's perfect.

scenarios.title: {BFf} Asks for a Loan
text: {BFf} messages: his motorbike was stolen and he needs it for work. He's embarrassed to ask. He asks.
{BFf} wants to open a small {FOOD} stall and needs money to start. He's sent a business plan. It's handwritten.

choices.label: Give it, not lend it
choices.text: {J} sends it with a note: 'Not a loan. Shut up.' {BFf} sends a voice note that is mostly silence.

choices.label: Lend it with a plan
choices.hint: Fair. Money and friends mix badly.

out.text: {BFf} pays back every cent, on time, with a thank-you note each month.
The payments stop after two months. Neither of them mentions it. It sits between them.

choices.label: Say you can't
choices.text: 'No worries, bro,' says {BFf}. The group chat is quieter after that.

scenarios.title: The Birthday Party
text: It's {BFf}'s birthday party back home. The whole old crew will be there. {J} has a match in four days.
An old friend is throwing a birthday party and has invited {J}. It's at {PLACE}. It'll go late. There will be phones.

choices.label: Go, leave early
choices.text: He arrives with a cake, stays two hours, leaves at ten. {BFf} hugs him at the door: 'You came.'

out.text: The best night in years. Nobody posts anything. The old crew protect their own.
A photo of {J} on a table at 3am makes the gossip accounts. The club is not impressed.

choices.label: Send a video message
choices.text: The video gets cheers. Then the party moves on without him, the way they increasingly do.

scenarios.title: {MUM} Comes to Visit
text: {MUM} has arrived for a week. She has brought two suitcases. One contains clothes. The other contains food, spices and a rice cooker.
{MUM}'s first visit abroad. She's never been on a plane before. She's holding the boarding pass like it might escape.
scenarios.prompt: How do you spend the week?

choices.label: Take her to the match
choices.hint: She'll cry. You'll play for her.
choices.text: She sits in the VIP section in her best clothes and cheers every time he touches the ball, even backwards passes. The club's media team film her. It's the best content they've ever had.

choices.label: Quiet week at home together
choices.text: The apartment smells like home for a week. He gains a kilo. The nutritionist sees it and says nothing, because he once had a mother too.

scenarios.title: A Taste of Home
text: {J} finds a tiny shop run by people from his country. The owner recognises him and refuses to take his money.
Homesick, {J} tries to cook {FOOD} from memory. It's wrong. It's almost right. He eats it anyway, standing at the counter.

choices.label: Become a regular
choices.text: The shop becomes his Sunday ritual. The owner's family adopt him. He gets a key to the back door.

choices.label: Call home while you eat
choices.text: He eats while {MUM} watches on video, critiquing his technique. It's the closest he's been to home in months.

scenarios.title: The Club Legend
text: A club legend, now sixty and walking with a stick, visits training. He watches {J} for twenty minutes and then waves him over.
The club's all-time top scorer is in the canteen. He asks, specifically, to meet {J}.

choices.label: 'What do you wish you'd known?'
choices.text: 'That it ends,' he says. 'Enjoy it more. Call your mother more. Save your money.' {J} writes all three down.

choices.label: 'Show me how you finished like that'
choices.text: The legend drops his stick and demonstrates a finish from 1987 with a shoe. It's still perfect. {J} copies it for an hour.

scenarios.title: The Lucky Socks
text: {J} realises he's won every match this month wearing the same pair of underwear. Unwashed. It's becoming a situation.
Since {J} started eating exactly three bananas before each game, the team hasn't lost. The bananas are now a squad matter.

choices.label: Never change it
choices.text: The ritual becomes squad lore. When it eventually stops working, they hold a small funeral for it.

choices.label: Break it deliberately
choices.text: He breaks it publicly. Half the squad is horrified. The other half respects the courage.

scenarios.title: A Handwritten Letter
text: A real letter, on paper, arrives at the club. It's from an eighty-year-old fan who has watched the club for seventy years. He writes that {J} reminds him of his late brother.
A letter in careful handwriting from a woman whose son was in hospital: he watched {J}'s games every week from his bed. He's better now. She wanted him to know.

choices.label: Write back by hand
choices.hint: Some things matter more than followers.
choices.text: It takes him an evening and four drafts. He never tells anyone he wrote it. The reply is framed in a living room he'll never see.

choices.label: Invite them to a match
choices.text: They come to a match. Afterwards he meets them in the tunnel. There's not a dry eye, including the security guard's.

scenarios.title: Somebody's Watching
text: {T} nudges {J} during the warm-up: there's a scout in the stand from a much bigger club, with a notebook and a very obvious club scarf.
{J}'s agent texts before training: 'Scouts in today. Don't change anything. Just be you.'

choices.label: Ignore it completely
choices.text: He doesn't look at the stand once. Afterwards, his agent says the scout wrote three pages.

out.text: A rabona, a flick, a bicycle kick that nearly works. The scout smiles. {Mf} doesn't.
He tries too hard and has his worst session of the month. The scout leaves at half-time.

scenarios.title: The Shirt Thief
text: After the match, a kid on the edge of the pitch is crying because a bigger boy grabbed the shirt {J} threw into the crowd.
Through the fence, {J} sees a small boy in a homemade shirt with his number drawn on in marker.

choices.label: Go back with another shirt
choices.text: He jogs back with a fresh shirt and signs it. The boy's face is something he'll remember for a long time.

choices.label: Invite the kid to training
choices.hint: The club's media team will love it.
choices.text: The boy comes to training, sits in the dugout, and gets nutmegged by the goalkeeper. Best day of his life.

scenarios.title: The Manager's Kid
text: {Mf}'s nine-year-old son is at training, and he's decided {J} is his favourite player. He follows {J} everywhere. {Mf} watches with an unreadable expression.
{Mf} brings his daughter to training. She asks {J} why he doesn't play every week. Out loud. In front of her father.

choices.label: Be a great role model
choices.hint: The manager is also a dad.
choices.text: He spends the afternoon showing the kid tricks. {Mf} says nothing, but the next day he says 'good morning' with his whole face.

choices.label: Answer the question honestly
choices.text: 'Ask your dad!' The kid does. {Mf} laughs for the first time in weeks. {J} still doesn't start on Sunday.

scenarios.title: Media Training
text: The club makes the young players attend media training. A former TV presenter fires trick questions at them. {J} is up next.
A media coach shows the squad clips of players saying terrible things in interviews. Then it's {J}'s turn in the hot seat.

choices.label: Take notes, practise
choices.text: He learns to pause, to bridge, to never repeat a negative question. The press team notice the difference immediately.

choices.label: Make everyone laugh
choices.text: His mock interview about 'eating the ball' has the squad in tears. The media coach writes 'needs work' on her clipboard.

scenarios.title: The Number Debate
text: The club's iconic number has become available. The kit man asks {J} if he wants it. It comes with history — and expectations.
A new signing has asked for {J}'s shirt number. Politely. With a smile. With the president standing next to him.

choices.label: Take the iconic number
choices.hint: Fans will love it. Or judge you for it.
choices.text: The announcement post is the club's most-liked of the season. Now he has to live up to it.

choices.label: Keep your own number
choices.text: He keeps his number. A small detail. Fans who notice respect it.

scenarios.title: Sunrise
text: {J} wakes up before dawn for no reason. The city is silent, purple and grey. His running shoes are by the door.
5:40am. Too early to be awake, too late to go back to sleep.

choices.label: Go for a sunrise run
choices.text: He runs by the water as the sun comes up. A street sweeper waves. For forty minutes, nothing is complicated.

choices.label: Stay in bed, watch the light
choices.text: He watches the light move across the ceiling and thinks about nothing at all. It's the most rested he's felt in weeks.

scenarios.title: The Team Quiz
text: It's quiz night on the team bus. {CAPl} reads questions from his phone. {J}'s team is losing badly, and the last round is 'general knowledge'.
The squad's monthly quiz. The prize is not having to carry the training equipment for a month.
scenarios.prompt: Final question: go for the big points?

ok.text: He's right. His team wins by one point. He's carried off the bus on shoulders. The cones will be carried by others.

bad.text: He's confidently, spectacularly wrong. The answer becomes a squad catchphrase.

choices.label: Let the clever one answer
choices.text: The reserve keeper, who reads books, answers correctly. {J} celebrates like he scored.

scenarios.title: A Message From an Old Rival
text: A message from a kid who bullied {J} at youth trials, years ago. He's working in a warehouse now. He writes that he's sorry, and that he watches every game.
The boy who beat {J} to a place in a youth team years ago sends a message: he never made it. He wants to say congratulations.

choices.label: Reply with grace
choices.text: They exchange long messages. It turns out they had more in common than either of them knew.

choices.label: Leave it on read
choices.text: He reads it twice and closes the app. That's allowed too.

scenarios.title: Another Patient
text: At the rehab clinic, a teenage boy in a wheelchair recognises {J}. He's recovering from a car accident. He asks how {J} stays motivated.
In the physio waiting room, an old man with a new hip asks {J} if footballers 'really cry this much about injuries'.

choices.label: Make a rehab pact
choices.text: They swap numbers and send each other their rehab progress every day. It becomes the thing that gets {J} out of bed.

choices.label: Quick chat and a photo
choices.text: A photo, some encouragement, a fist bump. Both of them feel a bit better.

scenarios.title: Dressing Room Gossip
text: The squad group chat lights up: rumour has it {Mf} is about to be sacked. Everyone is speculating. Screenshots are flying.
A teammate forwards {J} a voice note claiming the club hasn't paid some of the staff. 'Don't share this,' it says, which means everyone has.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.text: He mutes the chat for a day. When the rumour turns out to be half wrong, he's glad he said nothing.

out.text: Twenty minutes of wild theories. Good fun, no harm done.
A screenshot of his message reaches {Mf}. Nobody knows how. Everybody knows how.

scenarios.title: A Child's Question
text: At a petrol station, a little girl tugs her father's sleeve and points at {J}. 'Daddy, is that the bad man from the news?' The father turns pale.
A boy wearing {J}'s shirt asks him, very seriously, whether what the papers said is true.

choices.label: Kneel down and talk to her
choices.text: 'Sometimes I make mistakes. I'm trying to be better.' The girl considers this and then asks for a photo. The father nods at him. It means a lot.

choices.label: Smile and walk away
choices.text: He walks away. The question follows him all day.

scenarios.title: The Showroom
text: A luxury car dealer invites {J} for a 'no-obligation test drive'. The car is {CAR}. The salesman is very, very good at his job.
{T} has a new car. It's absurd. {J} sits in it and feels something dangerous.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.text: He drives it home grinning. {BFf} screams down the phone. {MUM} asks how much it cost and goes silent at the answer.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: He hands back the keys. The salesman gives him a card 'for when you're ready'. The card stays on his fridge.

scenarios.title: The Proposal
text: A fan emails the club: he wants to propose to his girlfriend at the training ground, and he wants {J} to hand him the ring.
A couple who met at one of {J}'s matches want him to be part of their proposal video.

choices.label: Yes, go all out
choices.text: He hands over the ring disguised as a match ball. She says yes. Then she asks for a selfie. The video gets two million views.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: He sends a signed card instead. The proposal still happens. He hopes they're happy.

scenarios.title: The Lookalike
text: There's a man who looks exactly like {J} getting free meals around town by pretending to be him. He's been doing it for a month. A restaurant owner calls the club.
A lookalike of {J} has 100,000 followers. He's doing ads. He's better at TikTok than {J} is.

choices.label: Meet him and film a video together
choices.hint: The internet will lose its mind.
choices.text: The video of the two of them confusing a waiter goes everywhere. The lookalike becomes a minor celebrity. {J} becomes a bigger one.

choices.label: Let the club's lawyers handle it
choices.text: A stern letter is sent. The lookalike posts it. The internet decides {J} is 'no fun'.

scenarios.title: The Old Team Photo
text: {DAD} sends a photo he found in a box: {J}'s first-ever team, aged nine, in shirts so big they're dresses. Half of the boys are tagged in the family chat.
Someone posts an old under-12 team photo. Of the sixteen boys in it, {J} is the only professional footballer.
scenarios.prompt: Reach out to the old team?

choices.label: Organise a reunion match
choices.text: Fourteen of the sixteen come. They lose 7-2 to a team of dads. It's the best afternoon of the year.

choices.label: Post it with a caption
choices.text: The post does huge numbers. Three of his old teammates comment. One of them is now a dentist.

scenarios.title: The First Real Suit
text: An awards dinner is coming up and {J} owns one suit, bought for a cousin's wedding when he was fifteen. A tailor offers to make him a proper one.
The club's sponsor provides suits for the squad. The tailor measures {J} and makes a small disappointed noise about his posture.

out.text: He makes the best-dressed list. Fashion accounts post about him. {MUM} is very proud.
He makes the worst-dressed list. The squad screenshots it into the group chat at 7am.

choices.label: Classic black
choices.text: Classic, sharp, forgettable. Exactly right.

scenarios.title: The Charity Auction
text: At a charity gala, {J}'s match-worn boots are up for auction. The bidding stalls at a humiliating number. Everyone is looking at him.
A gala dinner. A signed shirt from {J} is lot 14. Lot 13, a holiday villa, went for a fortune. The room is quiet.

choices.label: Bid on your own boots
choices.text: {J} raises his own paddle and bids {cost}. The room erupts. The video of it raises more than the boots.

choices.label: Add a training session to the lot
choices.text: 'Plus a training session with me.' The bidding explodes. The winner is a nine-year-old with his father's credit card.

scenarios.title: One Umbrella
text: {WEATHER} outside {PLACE}. {J} has an umbrella. An old woman at the bus stop does not.
Rain hammers down. A delivery rider is sheltering under a tiny awning, soaked, phone dying, order going cold.

choices.label: Give away the umbrella
choices.text: He arrives at training drenched. The physio thinks he's mad. He feels great.

choices.label: Offer a lift
choices.text: Twenty minutes of conversation with a stranger who has no idea who he is. It's the most normal he's felt in months.

scenarios.title: The Coffee Run
text: As the youngest and least-used member of the squad, {J} is told to do the coffee run. Thirty-one orders. Several involve oat milk. One involves 'whatever, surprise me'.
Squad tradition: the player with the fewest minutes buys the coffee. It's {J}. Again.

choices.label: Do it perfectly
choices.text: Thirty-one coffees, all correct. {CAPl} raises his cup to him. Small things build reputations.

choices.label: Get everyone the same thing
choices.text: Thirty-one identical espressos. Outrage, then laughter. The court fines him, but he becomes a legend.

scenarios.title: Named After You
text: A couple at the gate hold up their newborn twins. One is named after {J}. The other is named after {CAPl}. They want a photo of all four.
A message to the club: a fan has named his baby boy after {J}. He attaches a photo. The baby looks unimpressed.

choices.label: Send a tiny signed shirt
choices.text: The baby wears the tiny shirt in every photo for a year. The family sends updates. {J} keeps every one.

choices.label: Post the photo
choices.text: The post is his most-loved ever. Three more babies are named after him that month.

scenarios.title: Holiday Plans
text: The season's over. Three weeks off. The squad is scattering to beaches. {MUM} wants him home. {BFf} wants a trip.
Summer break. The fitness coach has given everyone a programme 'for the holiday'. Nobody has looked at it.

choices.label: Home to family
choices.text: Three weeks of home: {MUM}'s food, {DAD}'s silence, {SIB}'s chaos. He comes back fat and happy.

out.text: Ten days of sun and laughter. Nobody recognises him. Perfect.
A tourist recognises him on a jet ski. The photos make the papers: 'Living the high life while his club struggles'.

choices.label: Stay and train privately
choices.text: He hires a private coach and trains twice a day. He comes back sharper than anyone, and slightly lonelier.

scenarios.title: The Players' Vote
text: The players' union sends out its award ballot. Players vote for the best player in the league. {J} can't vote for himself. He can vote for {T}, his friend, or for the obvious winner from {R}.
Ballot time. The players' awards. {J} has to choose between loyalty and honesty.

choices.label: The best player, honestly
choices.text: He votes honestly. Nobody will ever know. He knows.

choices.label: Your teammate
choices.text: {T} somehow finds out and hugs him at training. The vote doesn't change the result, but it changes something.

scenarios.title: The Mirror
text: In the dressing-room mirror, after everyone's gone, {J} looks at himself for a long time.
{J} catches his reflection in a shop window and doesn't like the tired, tense person looking back.

choices.label: 'You've survived worse.'
choices.text: He thinks of the 5am buses to trials, the rejection letters, the borrowed boots. He has survived worse. He'll survive this.

choices.label: Book a session with the club psychologist
choices.text: The psychologist is calm and asks good questions. It's the first of many sessions. It helps more than he expected.

scenarios.title: An Embarrassing Injury
text: {J} has hurt his toe. Not in training. Not in a match. On a coffee table, at home, in the dark. The physio wants to know how. The squad wants to know more.
{J} pulled a muscle reaching for the TV remote. It's minor. The story is not.

choices.label: Tell the truth
choices.text: He tells the truth. The squad buys him a padded coffee table. The club's social team posts about it. He'll never live it down.

choices.label: 'Training knock'
choices.text: 'Training knock.' The physio winks. The kit man knows. By Friday everyone knows.

scenarios.title: Doorstepped
text: A reporter and a photographer are waiting outside {J}'s building at 7am. They want a comment on 'the rumours'. He hasn't heard the rumours.
A tabloid photographer is camped outside {J}'s apartment. A reporter shouts questions as he gets into his car.

choices.label: Stop, smile, say 'no comment'
choices.text: He smiles, says 'no comment, have a good day', and leaves. The photos are so boring they're never printed.

choices.label: Tell them to leave
choices.text: The photo of him pointing angrily is on the front page the next morning: '{J} Snaps'.

choices.label: Offer them coffee
choices.text: He brings them two coffees. They're so confused they leave. The reporter's piece the next week is noticeably softer.
